brief_summary: Two-row horizontal bar comparison of pin counts for wiring the same 104-key board: direct per-switch wiring (one pin per switch plus a shared ground) versus an 8-row by 13-column matrix (8 row pins + 13 column pins). The matrix bar is drawn far shorter and coral-highlighted to show the pin-count savings for an identical key count.
data_sources: key-matrix-ghosting-deep-dive.mdx § 'Wiring a grid instead of a wire per key' — 'Lay that same 104-key board out as 8 rows by 13 columns — 8 × 13 = 104, so every switch still gets a unique address — and the controller needs only 21 pins: eight for the rows, thirteen for the columns.'
https://develop-docs.qmk.fm/how_a_matrix_works — 'Without a matrix circuit, each switch would require its own wire directly to the controller.'
